solution overview

oracle database is a relational database from oracle. the solution is designed to manage and store information. oracle database is much more than a database. it also consists of management capabilities to secure and audit sensitive data, as well as capabilities for high availability and recoverability. the oracle database also has significant performance-related features and tools to analyze and report on data stored in the database. additionally, the system supports various business intelligence operations, analytics operations, and transaction processing. there are many versions of the oracle database, each subsequent version being an enhanced version of its predecessor. besides its database products, oracle has numerous applications in the business world, like e-business suite (ebs), peoplesoft, and jd edwards. they also have developer tools and application middleware software, as well as hardware and engineered systems for a variety of needs. x click here for a quick oracle refresher. oracle poweredge architecture overview

important terminology server: a physical or virtual server running oracle database software instance: oracle database software running on a server oracle database: data file that contains the actual data being stored in the database application: business application accessing database instances oracledb workload: structured query language requests made by users through applications physical virtual oracle db pe oracle server power bireport server user oracledb 101010010100011101010101001110101010111011001010101 101010010100011101010101001110101010111011001010101 101010010100011101010101001110101010111011001010101 101010010100011101010101001110101010111011001010101 architecture overview commonoracle / poweredge architectures oracle terminology commonoracle terminology commonoracle terminology industry terminology oracle terminology keycustomerphrases oracle deal technologies solutions implementations masteryoforacleterminology trustedadvisor oracle database terminology

customers often use copies of the production database for application development and testing, or devtest. many times, due to the application requirements, the entire database must be copied or cloned from production environments to devtest systems. storage arrays that have deduplication and compression capabilities help to dramatically reduce the storage space consumed by the devtest database copies. it is important to remove or mask any personal identifiable information, or pii, attributes before it is shared with application devtest teams. tools like appsync can help with cloning from production to devtest. additionally, appsync can run a customer-built script to perform data masking of the pii. devtest x if the word archive comes up in a conversation with an oracle customer, it usually refers to moving old, rarely accessed application data from the source database to another database, or to some other type of data structure, like flat files. then the archived data is purged or deleted from the source database. common reasons to use an archive/purge strategy are to reduce the: storage consumption of the database related backup space consumed dr storage space copies database clone storage space copies and latency of queries that do full table or full table partition scans tiering means moving less frequently used data from more expensive, higher performing media to lower-cost media with lower performance metrics, yet keeping the tiered data in the same database archive/purge and tiering x when an oracle customer talks about server consolidation, they usually mean moving multiple database instances onto a single server in order to run multiple oracle database instances simultaneously on the same physical host. when a customer talks about database consolidation, they mean combining the data from multiple databases, so the data is stored in a single database on a server. consolidation x occasionally, a customer might want to change the os platform of the database; for example, changing from aix to linux. this is called a platform migration and typically requires application and database downtime due to the way the bit-level data are encoded and written to the database data files on storage. migration x an oracle database upgrade implies running the upgrade scripts for a new version of oracle database software with the intent of converting an existing oracle database to a newer version. this is an upgrade of the oracle software; data files in the database are not impacted. upgrade x additional terminology migration migration migration migration consolidation consolidation consolidation consolidation upgrade upgrade upgrade upgrade devtest devtest devtest devtest archivepurgetiering archivepurgetiering archivepurgetiering archivepurgetiering deploy deploy click each term for a description.

oracle software used to simplify and streamline the process of performing database and log file backups, as well as executing a restore/recovery process; also used to clone a database from prod to devtest recovery manager (rman) x oracle’s cloud offering, where the application and databases run either in oracle’s public cloud site or on-premises at the customer site oracle cloud infrastructure (oci) x a licensed option for oracle databases. aco is used to perform host-based compression of the database data. it reduces the amount of space consumed in the database block, which enables the database to write more rows in a database block. this can help improve performance and reduce the size of the database host buffer cache. advanced compression option (aco) x a licensed option for oracle databases. tde is used to perform host-based encryption of the database data. it provides in-flight and at rest encryption of database data. transparent data encryption (tde) x an engineered solution from oracle that contains compute, connectivity, storage, and special storage io reduction capabilities called smart scan and storage indexes exadata x dashboards, apis, and other capabilities to manage and monitor a customer’s various oracle database implementations oracle enterprise manager (oem) x a database-level tool used to replicate database changes to another database common use cases for the replicated database changes include reporting, os platform migration to reduce system downtime, data recovery (dr), devtest operations, moving data from oracle to sql server, and more. goldengate x x a remote replication solution used to replicate changes from the primary database and apply them to a remote, standby database running on another server and storage array, mostly in a remote dr site data guard oracle’s filesystem and volume manager built into the database kernel starting in version 10g, circa 1996 automated storage management (asm) x an active-active server clustering capability that allows multiple hosts, such as database instances, to concurrently read and write to the same single database on storage. real application cluster (rac) x oracle disk configuration best practices summary oracle’s guidance for the configuration of database storage is to separate data files from log files. data files should be placed on data disks redo log files should go on redo disks and archive log files should reside on fast recovery area disks use raid 5 next best practices for oracle disk resources business-critical db provide dedicated luns for certain file types. performance analysis performance tuning io scalability space scaling dedicated luns data files online redo log files archive files snap the db recommended raid configurations all-flash storage dram cache back-end connectivity recommended best practice: raid 10 raid 5 caution: old documentation is based on old and slow technology.
